scenes.title: Statement and Proof
scenes.summary: A speech has two necessary parts: the statement of its subject and the proof of it. Narration belongs to judicial speech alone, and replies to the opponent, comparison and recapitulation only where there is a dispute, so at most a speech has four parts: proem, statement, proof and epilogue.

scenes.title: Needless Divisions
scenes.summary: To divide further, as the school of Theodorus did, into narration, supplementary narration and preliminary narration, refutation and further refutation, is empty and silly, like the names Licymnius invented in his Art.
